description_full: Nordson Corporation engineers, manufactures, and markets products and systems to dispense, apply, and control adhesives, coatings, polymers, sealants, biomaterials, medical components, and other fluids. The Industrial Precision Solutions segment provides dispensing, coating, and laminating systems for adhesives, lotions, liquids, and fibers to disposable products and roll goods; automated adhesive dispensing systems; components and systems for thermoplastic and biopolymer melt stream; fluid components, such as nozzles, pumps, and filters; smart components that measure and control the flow, quantity and location of dispensed fluid; control systems; and product assembly solutions. It also offers automated and manual dispensing products and systems for cold materials, container coating, liquid finishing, and powder coating, as well as ultraviolet equipment. The Medical and Fluid Solutions segment offers precision manual and semi-automated dispensers, plastic molded syringes, cartridges, tips, and fluid connection components; interventional solutions for engineered shafts and interventional delivery systems, medical tubing, balloons, balloon inflators, nitinol devices, cardiovascular cannula, and biomaterial delivery; medical fluid components; and microplegia myocardial protection devices and related consumables. The Advanced Technology Solutions segment provides automated dispensing systems for high-speed, precise application of various attachment, protection, and coating fluids, and related gas plasma treatment systems; destructive and non-destructive testing technologies, such as bond testers and automated optical, acoustic microscopy, and x-ray inspection systems used in the semiconductor and printed circuit board industries; and precision measurement and control technologies. The company markets its products through direct sales force, distributors, and sales representatives. Nordson Corporation was founded in 1909 and is headquartered in Westlake, Ohio.

CEO compensation is 7× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (6/10).
financial_summary: Nordson Corporation is a large-cap industrials business with a $17.3B market cap on $2.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +3% over the past three years and +5% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 15% against a 9% cost of capital, a 6-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $661M in free cash flow — roughly 24 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.48× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.4× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 6.8×.

Shareholder yield of 2.8% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 2.3× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 25% operating margin runs 17pp above the Industrials median (9%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 2.32x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+2.7% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.01 across 544 companies in the universe; the top four hold 9% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 47% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 9% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 23% and a beta of 1.01, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.51 vs 5y 1.01), so read it loosely.
Liquidity is deep, with about $111.0M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 44% in the 2020 crash, 22% in the 2022 bear market and 74% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $229 (margin of safety -36%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 24%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $175 to $304 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Industrials peers: P/E 31.4 vs 23.3 and EV/EBITDA 19.8 vs 13.3 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 37% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 3.8% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 3.7% (vs the 8% bar).
The 7 covering analysts target $350 on average, 13% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 15% earns above the cost of capital of 9.2%, but the 6pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.42).
It converts 24% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 1.48x.
ROE of 16% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.9x equity multiplier).
It spends 2.4% of revenue on R&D and 0.7% on stock compensation.
hlth: Leverage is moderate at 2.4x net debt to EBITDA ($108.4M of cash against $2.0B of debt), above the 1.5x gate, with interest covered 6.8x.
Working capital ties up about 171 days of sales, a drag on cash generation.
Goodwill makes up 56% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 2.5% over 3 years, 5.6% over 5 years and 5.2% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 7.9% a year over five years.
Capex runs only 0.7x depreciation (2.1% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 29, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 2.5% on average.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.3%), and institutions hold 78%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (5 sales, net $876K sold).
It returns 2.8% a year to shareholders (1.7% in buybacks and 1.2% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 0.8% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
It has paid a dividend for 39 consecutive years, raising it 15.2% a year over the last five.
people: With about 8,200 employees, each generates about $340K of revenue, in line with the Industrials median, and productivity has risen 6.8% a year.
That works out to $81K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.4M (7x revenue per employee).
